addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- qemu-runner: Use this agent when you need to run a RISC-V ELF binary through Andes QEMU and get its output. Always use this agent instead of running QEMU directly, as it handles the semihosting fd 9 output capture quirk in Claude Code's sandbox.

Examples:

- assistant: *builds a test binary*
  assistant: "Let me use the qemu-runner agent to execute the binary and check the output"

- user: "Run this ELF at VLEN=512"
  assistant: "I'll use the qemu-runner agent to run it" (Tools: Bash, Read) (Tools: Bash)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by running the app and observing behavior. Use when asked to verify a PR, confirm a fix works, test a change manually, check that a feature works, or validate local changes before pushing.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

aiTitle: 確認 Verilator 建置所需檔案

content.text:
`include/hybrid` 是 QEMU plugin、vsim、driver 三方共用的 ABI 合約。對「build verilator」來說，需要的是其中一部分:

| Header | vsim binary (`src/`) | vsim unit tests | 誰還在用 |
|---|---|---|---|
| `state_abi.h` | ✅ | ✅ | plugin, driver |
| `state_abi_check.h` | ✅ (被 `state_abi.h` 在 L117 include) | ✅ | plugin |
| `insn_match.h` | ✅ (`csr_trigger.hpp`, `handoff_controller.hpp`) | ✅ | plugin |
| `handoff_site.h` | ❌ | ✅ (只有 test) | plugin |
| `v_drain_policy.h` | ❌ | ✅ (只有 test) | plugin |
| `reg_names.h` | ❌ | ❌ | **只有** plugin |

- 只 build **vsim 執行檔** → 3 個: `state_abi.h` + `state_abi_check.h` + `insn_match.h`
- 連 **unit tests** 一起 build → 再加 `handoff_site.h`、`v_drain_policy.h`，共 5 個
- `reg_names.h` verilator 完全不用 (只有 QEMU plugin 用)

---

## 關於「移出 verilator」

先講現況: `verilator/` **已經是 submodule** 了 (`.gitmodules` → `hybrid_vsim`)。真正的問題是它的 build 反向往上抓 parent 的 header:

```
verilator/CMakeLists.txt:455
    "${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/../include"   <- 伸手進 andesim 的 include/hybrid
```

submodule 往上抓 superproject 的檔案,是 git 的反模式 (anti-pattern)。所以 verilator **沒辦法單獨 build**。要乾淨地「移出」,就要切斷這條往上的線。

但 `include/hybrid` 不能直接搬進 verilator —— 因為 QEMU plugin (產生端) 和 driver 也要用它。把合約塞進「消費端」的 repo,等於讓生產者反過來依賴消費者,方向是錯的。

1	// Pattern recogniser for the magic handoff marker convention. The same
2	// predicate runs in two places: the QEMU TCG plugin (C) and the vsim PC
3	// pre-scan (C++).
4	//
5	// The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions: SLTI with rd=x0 discards its
6	// result, so it is an architectural NOP on every conforming core. Marker
7	// binaries therefore run unmodified on real silicon and on every engine
8	// (fast/cycle/hybrid) -- unlike the retired `csrwi 0x7C0` markers, where
9	// CSR 0x7C0 is MILMB on Andes cores and the exit marker enabled ILM at
10	// base 0, killing standalone runs. The 12-bit immediate carries the
11	// marker kind; rs1 is pinned to x0 so each marker is one exact 32-bit
12	// word. SLTI has no compressed form, so markers are always 4 bytes.
13	
14	#ifndef HYBRID_INSN_MATCH_H
15	#define HYBRID_INSN_MATCH_H
16	
17	#include <stdbool.h>
18	#include <stdint.h>
19	
20	#ifdef __cplusplus
21	extern "C" {
22	#endif
23	
24	typedef enum
25	{
26	  HYBRID_HANDOFF_NONE  = 0,
27	  HYBRID_HANDOFF_ENTER = 1,  // slti x0, x0, 0x5A0
28	  HYBRID_HANDOFF_EXIT  = 2,  // slti x0, x0, 0x5A1
29	} hybrid_handoff_kind;
30	
31	// slti x0, x0, imm: OP-IMM (0x13), funct3=010, rd=rs1=x0, imm[31:20].
32	#define HYBRID_MARKER_ENTER_INSN 0x5A002013u
33	#define HYBRID_MARKER_EXIT_INSN  0x5A102013u
34	
35	// Returns true when `insn` is one of the two marker HINTs. On match,
36	// *out_kind is set to ENTER or EXIT.
37	static inline bool hybrid_match_handoff_insn(uint32_t insn,
38	                                             hybrid_handoff_kind* out_kind)
39	{
40	  if (insn == HYBRID_MARKER_ENTER_INSN) {
41	    *out_kind = HYBRID_HANDOFF_ENTER;
42	    return true;
43	  }
44	  if (insn == HYBRID_MARKER_EXIT_INSN) {
45	    *out_kind = HYBRID_HANDOFF_EXIT;
46	    return true;
47	  }
48	  return false;
49	}
50	
51	#ifdef __cplusplus
52	}  // extern "C"
53	#endif
54	
55	#endif  // HYBRID_INSN_MATCH_H

/* B7: pure decision function for the QEMU plugin V-state drain gate.
 *
 * The plugin uses one `qemu_plugin_register*` handle per architectural V
 * register. Each handle is non-NULL iff the gdbstub feature XML
 * advertised that register at plugin init. The original gate at
 * hybrid_handoff.c:296 tested `if (v->vlenb && s.vlenb > 0)` which
 * silently omits the V block when:
 *   - vlenb was not advertised but vtype/vl were (partial V), or
 *   - vlenb was advertised but read as zero (V disabled at runtime).
 *
 * Mixing the "stub broke" case with the "V disabled" case loses
 * information; the partial-advertisement case should refuse rather than
 * pretend V is absent (the resume side then mis-restores).
 *
 * This header is pure C, no QEMU plugin dependency, so it can be unit-
 * tested from a host C++ doctest.
 */
#ifndef HYBRID_V_DRAIN_POLICY_H
#define HYBRID_V_DRAIN_POLICY_H

#include <stdint.h>

#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"  /* HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX: the L11 ceiling */

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

typedef enum {
    HYBRID_V_DRAIN_OK = 0,      /* proceed: copy full V block into state */
    HYBRID_V_DRAIN_SKIP = 1,    /* no V at all; do not set HYBRID_FLAG_V */
    HYBRID_V_DRAIN_ABORT = 2,   /* partial advertisement; refuse to drain */
} HybridVDrainPolicy;

/* Decide whether to drain the V block.
 *
 * has_vlenb:    1 iff the stub advertised the vlenb register handle.
 * has_other_v:  1 iff ANY of vtype/vl/vstart/vxsat/vxrm/vcsr/vreg[*] was
 *               advertised (i.e. some V state is visible).
 * vlenb_value:  the value read from vlenb (only meaningful when has_vlenb).
 */
static inline HybridVDrainPolicy
hybrid_v_drain_policy(int has_vlenb, int has_other_v, uint64_t vlenb_value)
{
    /* Truth table (see v_drain_policy.test.cpp):
     *   has_vlenb=0, has_other_v=0            -> SKIP   (no V)
     *   has_vlenb=0, has_other_v=1            -> ABORT  (partial advertisement)
     *   has_vlenb=1, has_other_v=0            -> SKIP   (nothing to drain)
     *   has_vlenb=1, has_other_v=1, vlenb=0   -> SKIP   (V disabled at runtime)
     *   has_vlenb=1, has_other_v=1, vlenb>MAX -> ABORT  (L11: wire format
     *                                            cannot hold this VLEN; never
     *                                            truncate silently)
     *   has_vlenb=1, has_other_v=1, otherwise -> OK
     */
    if (!has_vlenb && has_other_v) return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_ABORT;
    if (!has_other_v)              return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_SKIP;
    if (vlenb_value == 0)          return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_SKIP;
    if (vlenb_value > HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX) return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_ABORT;
    return HYBRID_V_DRAIN_OK;
}

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif  /* HYBRID_V_DRAIN_POLICY_H */

# andes-hybrid-abi

The shared wire-format contract for the Andes hybrid RISC-V simulator. These
headers define the bytes exchanged across the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. They are
consumed by three independent components, so they live in their own repo and
are pinned as a submodule by each consumer (one source of truth, no drift):

| Consumer | Repo | Mounts this as |
|----------|------|----------------|
| `andesim` (QEMU TCG plugin + C++ driver) | top repo | `include/` |
| `hybrid_vsim` (vsim / SystemC + Verilator) | submodule | `external/hybrid-abi/` |

Both mount points put this repo's root on the include path, so every consumer
includes the same way:

```c
#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
```

## Layout

```
hybrid/
  state_abi.h        struct hybrid_state_v1 -- the wire format
  state_abi_check.h  compile-time offset/size lock (static_assert)
  insn_match.h       handoff marker HINT recogniser
  handoff_site.h     translate-time trigger capture + post-trigger PC
  v_drain_policy.h   pure V-state drain gate decision
  reg_names.h        GDB register-name tables (gdbstub wire contract)
tests/
  abi_compile_check.{c,cpp}  include every header from C and C++
  check.sh                   compile both as C11 + C++20
```

## Contract rules

- Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host). Not
  endian-portable.
- Never repurpose offsets within a published version. Add fields by consuming
  bytes from `reserved`, or bump to v2. `state_abi_check.h` locks every offset;
  a layout change must update it in lock-step and bump `HYBRID_STATE_VERSION`.
- Both C and C++ must keep compiling these headers.

## Test

```sh
tests/check.sh        # host gcc/g++, zero external deps
```

A pass means the headers are self-contained from the repo root and the
`hybrid_state_v1` layout matches the locked offsets.

## History

Started fresh at the submodule split; the pre-split history of these headers
lives in the `andesim` repo under `include/hybrid/`.

# ROADMAP: split the shared ABI into its own repo, decouple verilator

## Goal

Make `verilator/` (the `hybrid_vsim` submodule) buildable on its own. Today its
CMake reaches UP into the parent at `../include` for the shared ABI headers --
a submodule depending on its superproject, the git anti-pattern. Extract
`include/hybrid/` into a standalone repo (`andes-hybrid-abi`) and pin it as a
submodule of BOTH `andesim` and `hybrid_vsim`. One source of truth; verilator
builds standalone.

## End state

```
andes-hybrid-abi/          NEW repo: root holds hybrid/<6 headers> + tests/
andesim/      (top repo)
  include/        -> submodule andes-hybrid-abi   (qemu_plugin + driver read here, unchanged paths)
  verilator/      -> submodule hybrid_vsim
       external/hybrid-abi -> submodule andes-hybrid-abi   (verilator reads here, builds alone)
  qemu_plugin/    HYBRID_INCLUDE ?= ../include    (unchanged)
  driver/         ../include                       (unchanged)
```

## Decisions (locked)

- ABI gets its OWN repo, submodule of both consumers (not vendored, not copied).
- Fresh git history (no filter-repo); pre-split history stays in andesim.
- `andesim/include/hybrid/*` include paths stay byte-identical -> ZERO source edits.
- Only build wiring changes: 2 verilator CMake lines + drop one Docker mount.
- User creates the empty Gitea repo; URL pending.

## Headers (the 6, who needs them)

- vsim binary needs: `state_abi.h` (+ `state_abi_check.h` transitively), `insn_match.h`
- vsim tests also need: `handoff_site.h`, `v_drain_policy.h`
- `reg_names.h`: only the QEMU plugin
- Moved as ONE unit (the whole `hybrid/` dir), not split.

## Features (one session each; update STATE as you go)

# ROADMAP: Andes HybridSim v1.0 (complete-all-features)

Single source of truth for everything required to ship Andes HybridSim
v1.0. Every feature traces to a functional requirement in `docs/FRS.md`,
which in turn traces to a market requirement in `docs/MRD.md`. Covering
all FRs therefore covers all MRs (FRS section 13 has no orphan).

This file **supersedes** two earlier engineering breakdowns, now in
`docs/archive/`:

- `docs/archive/commercial_v1_roadmap.md` - Waves 0-6 closing L1-L21
- `docs/archive/TODO.md` - failure-mode backlog F-T1.1..F-T3.8

Their content is absorbed below as full feature entries. `docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb`
stays as the plain-English "do not do this" envelope and the L-id source.

House rules (from `CLAUDE.md`): one session completes one feature. Update
the feature's Status when starting (in-progress) and on completion (done).
Each code feature carries a TDD RED line: the failing test you write first.

## Status legend

- not-started: no work yet
- in-progress: being implemented in a session
- partial: shipped for the M-mode envelope, incomplete for the full FR
- done: behavioural + structural commits landed, tests pass
- business: not a code task; a sign-off / process / legal deliverable

## Feature ID scheme

- `F-ENG-*` - engineering: ROI-envelope and correctness of the cycle engine
- `F-PROD-*` - productization: interfaces, trace, observability, encryption,
  licensing, packaging
- `F-BIZ-*` - business / legal / process: tagged `business`, no TDD RED

---

# ROADMAP: split the shared ABI into its own repo, decouple verilator

Scope: build-system restructuring only. Separate from the product
`ROADMAP.md` (the v1.0 FR tracker) -- this touches no FR, only git layout.

## Goal

Make `verilator/` (the `hybrid_vsim` submodule) buildable on its own. Today its
CMake reaches UP into the parent at `../include` for the shared ABI headers --
a submodule depending on its superproject, the git anti-pattern. Extract
`include/hybrid/` into a standalone repo (`andes-hybrid-abi`) and pin it as a
submodule of BOTH `andesim` and `hybrid_vsim`. One source of truth; verilator
builds standalone.

## End state

```
andes-hybrid-abi/          NEW repo: root holds hybrid/<6 headers> + tests/
andesim/      (top repo)
  include/        -> submodule andes-hybrid-abi   (qemu_plugin + driver read here, unchanged paths)
  verilator/      -> submodule hybrid_vsim
       external/hybrid-abi -> submodule andes-hybrid-abi   (verilator reads here, builds alone)
  qemu_plugin/    HYBRID_INCLUDE ?= ../include    (unchanged)
  driver/         ../include                       (unchanged)
```

## Decisions (locked)

- ABI gets its OWN repo, submodule of both consumers (not vendored, not copied).
- Fresh git history (no filter-repo); pre-split history stays in andesim.
- `andesim/include/hybrid/*` include paths stay byte-identical -> ZERO source edits.
- Only build wiring changes: 2 verilator CMake lines + drop one Docker mount.
- User creates the empty Gitea repo; URL pending.

## Headers (the 6, who needs them)

- vsim binary needs: `state_abi.h` (+ `state_abi_check.h` transitively), `insn_match.h`
- vsim tests also need: `handoff_site.h`, `v_drain_policy.h`
- `reg_names.h`: only the QEMU plugin
- Moved as ONE unit (the whole `hybrid/` dir), not split.

## Features (one session each; update STATE as you go)

### F1 -- create andes-hybrid-abi repo
- STATE: STAGED (content + self-test green in scratchpad; pending Gitea URL to push)
- Desc: new repo, root `hybrid/` = the 6 headers byte-exact, `tests/check.sh`
  compiles them as C11 + C++20 with the layout static_asserts firing, README.
- Verify: `tests/check.sh` -> "abi-compile-check OK" (passing in scratchpad now)
- Blocks on: Gitea URL (to set origin + push fresh initial commit)

### F2 -- andesim: include/ becomes a submodule
- STATE: TODO
- Desc: `git rm -r include` (the tracked dir), `git submodule add <url> include`.
- Key files: `.gitmodules`, `include/` (mode 160000)
- Verify: `make -C qemu_plugin` green; driver build green; headers identical.
- Depends on: F1 (needs the pushed repo URL)

### F3 -- verilator: external/hybrid-abi submodule + swap include paths
- STATE: TODO
- Desc: in the hybrid_vsim repo, `git submodule add <url> external/hybrid-abi`;
  change `../include` -> `external/hybrid-abi` in CMakeLists.txt:455 and
  cmake/HybridConfig.cmake:14; drop the `-v $ROOT/include:/include:ro` mount in
  andesim `scripts/build_vsim.sh` (headers now in-tree under /work/external).
- Key files: `verilator/.gitmodules`, `verilator/CMakeLists.txt`,
  `verilator/cmake/HybridConfig.cmake`, `scripts/build_vsim.sh`
- Verify: verilator builds STANDALONE (clone + submodule init + build, no parent
  include/ present) AND via `scripts/build_vsim.sh`.
- Depends on: F1

### F4 -- full-chain validation
- STATE: TODO
- Desc: bump verilator submodule pointer in andesim; build + test everything.
- Verify: `bash scripts/build_all.sh` green; `JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`
  green; driver parity `tests/andes_sim/parity.sh` green; cycle figures
  unchanged vs a pre-split baseline.
- Depends on: F2, F3

### F5 -- publish
- STATE: TODO
- Desc: confirm Gitea URLs in both `.gitmodules`; push abi repo, push hybrid_vsim
  submodule bump, push andesim. Verify a fresh `git clone --recursive` builds.
- Verify: clean-clone `--recursive` -> `build_all.sh` green.
- Depends on: F4

## Notes

- Nested submodule: andes-hybrid-abi appears twice (andesim/include and
  andesim/verilator/external/hybrid-abi). Both pin the SAME commit; keep them in
  step when the ABI changes (bump abi -> bump in verilator -> bump verilator in
  andesim).
- `scripts/build_vsim.sh` currently mounts `$ROOT/include:/include:ro` so the
  container's `/work/../include` resolves. After F3 that mount is dead code.
- Staged F1 content lives in the session scratchpad until the URL arrives.

# andesim_abi

The shared wire-format contract for the Andes hybrid RISC-V simulator. These
headers define the bytes exchanged across the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. They are
consumed by three independent components, so they live in their own repo and
are pinned as a submodule by each consumer (one source of truth, no drift):

| Consumer | Repo | Mounts this as |
|----------|------|----------------|
| `andesim` (QEMU TCG plugin + C++ driver) | top repo | `include/` |
| `hybrid_vsim` (vsim / SystemC + Verilator) | submodule | `external/andesim_abi/` |

Both mount points put this repo's root on the include path, so every consumer
includes the same way:

```c
#include "hybrid/state_abi.h"
```

## Layout

```
hybrid/
  state_abi.h        struct hybrid_state_v1 -- the wire format
  state_abi_check.h  compile-time offset/size lock (static_assert)
  insn_match.h       handoff marker HINT recogniser
  handoff_site.h     translate-time trigger capture + post-trigger PC
  v_drain_policy.h   pure V-state drain gate decision
  reg_names.h        GDB register-name tables (gdbstub wire contract)
tests/
  abi_compile_check.{c,cpp}  include every header from C and C++
  check.sh                   compile both as C11 + C++20
```

## Contract rules

- Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host). Not
  endian-portable.
- Never repurpose offsets within a published version. Add fields by consuming
  bytes from `reserved`, or bump to v2. `state_abi_check.h` locks every offset;
  a layout change must update it in lock-step and bump `HYBRID_STATE_VERSION`.
- Both C and C++ must keep compiling these headers.

## Test

```sh
tests/check.sh        # host gcc/g++, zero external deps
```

A pass means the headers are self-contained from the repo root and the
`hybrid_state_v1` layout matches the locked offsets.

## History

Started fresh at the submodule split; the pre-split history of these headers
lives in the `andesim` repo under `include/hybrid/`.
